ca_parking_lot_rocks.blurb: Parking Lot Rocks is a small crag in the Forty Nine Palms Oasis area of Joshua Tree National Park, just east of Indian Cove on the Highway 62 side of the park. It holds seven routes across trad, sport and a single top-rope line, running from 5.5 to 5.9, with most falling between 5.7 and 5.9. A few lines start beside the car park, and the rest climb the steep hillside to the south. The stone is quartz monzonite. This is a short-outing stop that pairs easily with a hike to the palm oasis nearby.
ca_parking_lot_rocks.parking_note: The Forty Nine Palms area is just east of Indian Cove and has its own entrance road and car park; the crag begins at that lot.

ca_9_chouinard.blurb: Chouinard is the far right sector of the main wall at Rush, in the June Lake area of the Eastern Sierra at roughly 7,400 feet. Its seven routes mix trad, sport and top-rope lines from 5.8 to 5.11. The wall is built of tall arêtes, faces and corners. Little climbing has happened here, so holds can be loose and breakable, and belayers should stand well clear of the base. Reaching the base means getting to the neighbouring Dostie sector first, then scrambling steeply up and to the right over dirt, grass and sagebrush. Most routes top out at the cliff edge, with rappel anchors available above.
